thesis: MongoDB's confirmed September 1 fiscal-Q2 2027 release reported 30% revenue growth, approximately 29% Atlas growth, positive operating income, nearly doubled free cash flow, and a higher full-year outlook. The raised outlook is meaningful positive counter-evidence; however, the current selloff followed third-quarter revenue guidance below the reported quarter and Atlas growth that did not accelerate, leaving the durability read unresolved, while Surman v. MongoDB has an October 5 court-ordered arbitration-status deadline. This supports avoiding a new entry pending clearer post-earnings demand evidence.
invalidation: Atlas growth accelerates, performance remains consistent with the raised outlook, the October litigation checkpoint creates no material overhang, and the post-earnings price-volume reaction stabilizes.
sources: Surman v. MongoDB July 9, 2026 court order: https://law.justia.com/cases/federal/district-courts/new-york/nysdce/1%3A2026cv00166/655879/24/

thesis: Sasol's audited FY2026 results, prepared under IFRS as issued by the IASB, reported issuer basic EPS of R18.99, 17% growth in adjusted EBITDA, 22% growth in operating cash generation, an 11% net-debt reduction, and five-year-high Secunda production, supporting a long thesis. The strongest negative counter-evidence is the absence of a final dividend while net debt remains above the policy threshold, an adverse internal-control opinion with open material weaknesses, and pending tax and environmental proceedings; however, the unqualified financial-statement audit and company-specific operating and balance-sheet improvements keep the net read positive. Conviction is medium because the result reflects several contributing operating and macro factors rather than one dominant driver.
invalidation: Net debt reverses higher, cash generation deteriorates, Secunda reliability weakens, or the open control deficiencies produce a confirmed restatement or qualified financial-statement opinion.

thesis: Harmony's confirmed FY2026 results, prepared under IFRS and IAS 34, reported production within guidance, record adjusted free cash flow, and a record dividend. Those cash and operating results are strong positive counter-evidence; however, the same filing corrected prior-period errors, restated comparative information, disclosed 19.5% to 24.5% life-of-mine reserve overstatements at three operations, and recalculated depreciation that had been understated from FY2020 through FY2026. The confirmed governance history and reduced reserve base support avoiding a new entry until the corrections and controls establish a clean track record.
invalidation: Independent reporting confirms sustained effective controls, corrected reserve planning remains stable without further adjustments, and subsequent operating results validate the revised mine plans.

thesis: Hess Midstream's confirmed August 3 second-quarter results reported $173.7 million of net income, $278.6 million of operating cash flow, a higher quarterly distribution, and reaffirmed full-year financial and throughput guidance, supporting a long thesis. The strongest counter-evidence is lower year-over-year revenue and declines in several throughput measures; however, a 56% capital-expenditure reduction, $231.6 million of issuer-defined adjusted free cash flow, and reaffirmed guidance show that lower activity has not displaced the cash-return plan. The latest Form 10-Q describes known legal outcomes as remote from material impact and effective controls, while the 2024 auditor change was disclosed as an independence consequence rather than a for-cause dismissal.
invalidation: The company withdraws guidance, stops distribution growth, or sustained throughput weakness reduces cash generation enough to impair the disclosed capital-return and deleveraging plan.
sources: SEC Hess Midstream August 3, 2026 earnings release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1789832/000119312526329567/hesm-ex99_1.htm
